vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-93994
vulnerability.description:
Apache MINA SSHD is a Java library for client-side and server-side SSH. SSH servers can be configured to require multi-authentication schemes, for instance two different public keys, not just one. In OpenSSH, this would be done by setting in sshd_config AuthenticationMethods "publickey,publickey". Apache MINA SSHD provides an equivalent configuration mechanism.




In Apache MINA SSHD versions up to 2.19.0 and 3.0.0-M1 to 3.0.0-M5 the server code in component sshd-core does not enforce that the two public keys presented are different. A user can thus successfully authenticate with only one of the two key pairs required by presenting this single key twice. This is a partial authentication bypass.






Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.20.0 or 3.0.0-M6, which fix this issue.

statements.status_notes: This flaw is a partial authentication bypass in Apache MINA SSHD's server-side multi-step authentication, where one public key can satisfy a two-key requirement; it needs an SSH server configured with that policy. The bundled Apache MINA SSHD 2.9.2 is not part of the SonarQube server runtime: it ships only inside the scanner engine, which the server provides as a download to scanners, and runs on the analysis machine. There it is used only as an optional SSH client for Subversion svn+ssh:// connections; no code in the scanner engine references the library's SSH server classes, so no SSH server is ever created and the vulnerable server-side code is never executed. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-93558
vulnerability.description: A flaw was found in Netty's WebSocketServerExtensionHandler. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by using HTTP/1.1 pipelining to send requests faster than the application can respond. This leads to an unbounded growth of a per-connection queue, consuming excessive memory. Eventually, this can cause the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) to exhaust its heap, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected server.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-93558 is a memory-exhaustion denial of service in Netty's WebSocketServerExtensionHandler when HTTP/1.1 requests are pipelined faster than they are answered. The bundled Elasticsearch HTTP listener installs no WebSocket handler. The only other classes in the product that reference Netty's WebSocket server classes belong to the Reactor Netty HTTP server in Elasticsearch's AI inference module, and nothing starts that server (the module uses Reactor Netty only as an outbound HTTP client). The vulnerable handler is never installed. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-93488
vulnerability.description: A flaw was found in Netty. SpdySessionHandler accepts an unlimited number of concurrent remote-initiated streams because localConcurrentStreams defaults to Integer.MAX_VALUE and the handler provides no API to change it. A remote peer can open a SPDY connection and send a large number of SYN_STREAM frames with FLAG_FIN=0, causing unbounded heap and direct memory allocation that can lead to JVM OutOfMemoryError and a denial of service.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-93488 is a denial of service in Netty's SpdySessionHandler, which accepts an unlimited number of concurrent SPDY streams; it only matters for an application that installs a SPDY handler. The bundled Elasticsearch HTTP listener builds each channel pipeline from Netty's HTTP/1.1 request decoder and response encoder, together with handlers for TLS, read timeouts, header validation, content decompression and compression, content size limits, flow control and request pipelining, none of which is a SPDY handler, and no class in the product outside Netty references Netty's SPDY package. SPDY is never negotiated or decoded. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-93491
vulnerability.description: A flaw was found in Netty's HttpServerCodec. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by pipelining HTTP/1.1 requests on a single connection and withholding reads. This action causes the methodOverflowQueue to grow without limit, leading to unbounded heap memory consumption and a denial of service due to memory exhaustion.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-93491 is a memory-exhaustion denial of service in Netty's HttpServerCodec, whose queue of pipelined request methods grows without limit. The bundled Elasticsearch HTTP listener does not use HttpServerCodec: its pipeline uses a separate HTTP/1.1 request decoder and response encoder. The only other classes in the product that reference HttpServerCodec belong to the Reactor Netty HTTP server in Elasticsearch's AI inference module, and nothing starts that server (the module uses Reactor Netty only as an outbound HTTP client). The vulnerable queue is never created. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-68498
vulnerability.description:
StreamReadConstraints.maxNameLength (default 50,000 characters) is intended to bound how much memory a single JSON Object property name can consume while being parsed, independently of the much larger maxStringLength (default 100,000,000 characters) that bounds ordinary string values. For parsers built over character input — Reader, String or char[] sources, all served by ReaderBasedJsonParser — that bound is not applied while the name is being accumulated. The code path instead re-uses the string-value length check, which is roughly 2000x larger by default.



In the character-input slow path, ReaderBasedJsonParser._parseName2() accumulates the name into the TextBuffer and, when a segment fills, calls TextBuffer.finishCurrentSegment(), which validates only maxStringLength. The correct check, StreamReadConstraints.validateNameLength(int), is reached afterwards in CharsToNameCanonicalizer.findSymbol(), once the entire name has been scanned to its closing quote. By that point the full name — up to maxStringLength characters — has already been buffered in memory.



A remote attacker who can have a single sufficiently long JSON Object property name parsed through this path can force allocation on the order of 100,000,000 characters (approximately 200 MB, with segment bookkeeping pushing real peak usage higher) before any StreamConstraintsException is thrown, instead of the approximately 50,000-character (about 100 KB) bound the API promises. Repeating this across concurrent requests can exhaust the heap and crash the process. No authentication or user interaction is required. Because StreamReadConstraints.maxDocumentLength is disabled by default (-1), nothing else bounds the token first, so the issue is exploitable under default configuration.



Byte-input parsers are not affected: UTF8StreamJsonParser, UTF8DataInputJsonParser and the non-blocking (async) parsers re-validate maxNameLength on every growth of the name-decode buffer via ParserBase._growNameDecodeBuffer(), rejecting an oversized name after allocating only tens of kilobytes. Applications are exposed when untrusted JSON is parsed from a String, Reader or char[] — for example an HTTP request body already read into a String — rather than from raw UTF-8 bytes.



This issue affects com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core from 2.16.0 and tools.jackson.core:jackson-core from 3.0.0. Releases before 2.16.0 are not affected, because StreamReadConstraints.maxNameLength was first introduced in jackson-core 2.16.0.

These copies are in the bundled Elasticsearch content parsing library (elasticsearch/lib/elasticsearch-x-content-9.4.7.jar). The limit this issue concerns is not enabled in Elasticsearch: its JSON parser factory (elasticsearch-x-content) sets both the maximum property name length and the maximum string length to 2147483647 for every JSON parser it creates, so Elasticsearch accepts property names of any length whichever encoding a request uses, and a jackson-core release that enforces the name limit earlier would not change that behaviour. vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-93568
vulnerability.description: A flaw was found in Netty. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 Extended CONNECT requests. Netty's HTTP-object conversion path incorrectly processes these requests as regular HTTP/1.1 CONNECT requests, leading to a loss of critical protocol and path information. This misinterpretation can allow attackers to bypass security policies, such as routing or authorization logic, in applications that rely on Netty for HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 communication, resulting in integrity loss.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-93568 is a flaw in Netty's HTTP/2 to HTTP/1 translation, where Extended CONNECT requests are downgraded as regular CONNECT requests; it matters only for a Netty server or proxy that converts requests received from an untrusted client. The netty-codec-http2 library is bundled only in Elasticsearch's AI inference module, where it is used by outbound HTTP clients (the AWS SDK client for Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker, and the Reactor Netty client behind the Azure SDK). Elasticsearch's own HTTP listener is HTTP/1.1 only, so no HTTP/2 connection is ever accepted. Those clients only send requests that Elasticsearch itself builds; no component converts requests received from another party with this code. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-93569

This inconsistency can allow an attacker to bypass security controls in Netty-based proxies or gateways, potentially leading to unauthorized access, cache poisoning, or misrouting of requests.

Those clients only send requests that Elasticsearch itself builds; no component converts requests received from another party with this code. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-93567
vulnerability.description: A flaw was found in Netty's HTTP/2 codec. When converting HTTP/1 CONNECT requests to HTTP/2, the component incorrectly uses the Host header instead of the CONNECT authority-form request-target for the tunnel authority. A remote attacker can exploit this by supplying a different Host header, leading to a malformed HTTP/2 CONNECT request. This can bypass security controls such as tunnel allow-lists or egress policies, resulting in integrity loss.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-93567 is a flaw in Netty's HTTP/1 to HTTP/2 translation, where an authority-form CONNECT request is converted with a Host-controlled :authority; it matters only for a Netty server or proxy that converts requests received from an untrusted client. The netty-codec-http2 library is bundled only in Elasticsearch's AI inference module, where it is used by outbound HTTP clients (the AWS SDK client for Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker, and the Reactor Netty client behind the Azure SDK). Elasticsearch's own HTTP listener is HTTP/1.1 only, so no HTTP/2 connection is ever accepted. Those clients only send requests that Elasticsearch itself builds; no component converts requests received from another party with this code. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-62243
vulnerability.description: Netty (io.netty:netty-handler) versions from 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.16.Final and versions through 4.1.136.Final disable TLS hostname verification on the SslProvider.OPENSSL client path when a plain (non-extended) X509TrustManager is used and Unsafe-based trust-manager wrapping is unavailable (Java 25+). In this configuration the OpenSSL client does not perform hostname verification, allowing a man-in-the-middle attacker to present a certificate issued for a different hostname that is accepted without validation. Fixed in 4.2.17.Final and 4.1.137.Final.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-62243 affects only Netty's OpenSSL-based TLS client (SslProvider.OPENSSL) used with a plain X509TrustManager, where hostname verification is skipped. That provider requires the separate netty-tcnative native library, which is not bundled anywhere in this edition, so these Netty copies can only use the JDK TLS engine, which is not affected. In this edition the bundled Elasticsearch also runs with TLS disabled on its own listeners, and the outbound clients in its AI inference module only choose OpenSSL when it is available. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-62380
vulnerability.description: Netty (io.netty:netty-codec-socks) versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.16.Final and 4.1.x through 4.1.136.Final contain null byte, CRLF, and credential injection vulnerabilities in the SOCKS4 (Socks4ClientEncoder) and SOCKS5 (Socks5ClientEncoder) client encoders, which fail to validate domain address and authentication (username/password) fields. An attacker able to control these fields can inject null bytes or CRLF characters to truncate or alter values, potentially enabling domain spoofing, SOCKS4 userid truncation, authentication data injection, and protocol confusion. Fixed in 4.2.17.Final and 4.1.137.Final.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-62380 is an input-validation flaw in Netty's SOCKS4 and SOCKS5 client encoders, exploitable only when an application opens a SOCKS proxy connection whose destination domain or proxy credentials are attacker-influenced. In this product the encoders are reachable only through the Azure SDK HTTP client in Elasticsearch's AI inference module, and only if a SOCKS proxy were configured for it: Elasticsearch passes no proxy settings to that client, and the Azure SDK's own proxy configuration loading only ever produces HTTP proxies, so the SOCKS encoders are never used. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-56855
vulnerability.description: Previously, after a channel has been established, a malicious peer could send crafted messages that would deadlock the entire connection. Now, we handle all RFC 4254 channel messages; global requests are handled explicitly. Then, treat all other messages as a protocol error and tear the connection down instead of buffering and blocking.

statements.status_notes: The vulnerability is in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package (handling of SSH channel messages on an established channel). The Helm template renderer bundled with the IaC analyzer links only the bcrypt, blowfish, pbkdf2 and scrypt packages of golang.org/x/crypto, pulled in by its template function library; an analysis of the bundled binaries for every platform (Linux, macOS and Windows) found no function from the ssh package and no SSH client, server or agent functionality. The vulnerable code is not part of the shipped binaries, which run on the analysis machine, not in the SonarQube server, and only render the Helm chart files of the analyzed project. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-78662
vulnerability.description: Previously, a channel registered in the mux's chanList is not usable until it is established. A malicious peer was able flood the channel's incomingRequests, deadlocking the entire connection. Now, we add an atomic established state, set when a channel becomes usable. Until such a time, handlePacket drops every packet other than the open confirmation/failure, without blocking and without tearing down the connection.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-56854
vulnerability.description: The source-address critical option in the Permissions returned by an authentication callback was only enforced for the PublicKeyCallback and VerifiedPublicKeyCallback paths, extending the fix for CVE-2026-46595. The check is now applied to the Permissions returned by any authentication callback.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-56624
vulnerability.description:
Improper certificate validation in Apache MINA SSHD (server-side). Apache MINA SSHD is a Java library for client-side and server-side SSH.




Server-side OpenSSH user certificate validation during user authentication in an Apache MINA SSHD server did not check for the unsupported force-command or verify-required options that could be embedded in the certificate, nor did it validate these options. As a result it was possible that a user could authenticate with such a certificate that included a force-command option but still was able to execute other commands. What other command exactly would be available to the user depends on the implementation of the server.




This issue is fixed in Apache MINA SSHD 2.19.0 and 3.0.0-M5. Applications are advised to upgrade to these versions.




The fix rejects OpenSSH user certificates that include these options, since Apache MINA SSHD implements neither force-command nor sk-*-cert-v01@openssh.com user certificates (which are the only ones for which verify-required would make sense).

The bundled Apache MINA SSHD 2.9.2 is not part of the SonarQube server runtime: it ships only inside the scanner engine, which the server provides as a download to scanners, and runs on the analysis machine. There it is used only as an optional SSH client for Subversion svn+ssh:// connections; no code in the scanner engine references the library's SSH server classes, so no SSH server is ever created and the vulnerable server-side code is never executed. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2023-48795
vulnerability.description: The SSH transport protocol with certain OpenSSH extensions, found in OpenSSH before 9.6 and other products, allows remote attackers to bypass integrity checks such that some packets are omitted (from the extension negotiation message), and a client and server may consequently end up with a connection for which some security features have been downgraded or disabled, aka a Terrapin attack. This occurs because the SSH Binary Packet Protocol (BPP), implemented by these extensions, mishandles the handshake phase and mishandles use of sequence numbers. For example, there is an effective attack against SSH's use of ChaCha20-Poly1305 (and CBC with Encrypt-then-MAC). The bypass occurs in chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com and (if CBC is used) the -etm@openssh.com MAC algorithms. This also affects Maverick Synergy Java SSH API before 3.1.0-SNAPSHOT, Dropbear through 2022.83, Ssh before 5.1.1 in Erlang/OTP, PuTTY before 0.80, AsyncSSH before 2.14.2, golang.org/x/crypto before 0.17.0, libssh before 0.10.6, libssh2 through 1.11.0, Thorn Tech SFTP Gateway before 3.4.6, Tera Term before 5.1, Paramiko before 3.4.0, jsch before 0.2.15, SFTPGo before 2.5.6, Netgate pfSense Plus through 23.09.1, Netgate pfSense CE through 2.7.2, HPN-SSH through 18.2.0, ProFTPD before 1.3.8b (and before 1.3.9rc2), ORYX CycloneSSH before 2.3.4, NetSarang XShell 7 before Build 0144, CrushFTP before 10.6.0, ConnectBot SSH library before 2.2.22, Apache MINA sshd through 2.11.0, sshj through 0.37.0, TinySSH through 20230101, trilead-ssh2 6401, LANCOM LCOS and LANconfig, FileZilla before 3.66.4, Nova before 11.8, PKIX-SSH before 14.4, SecureCRT before 9.4.3, Transmit5 before 5.10.4, Win32-OpenSSH before 9.5.0.0p1-Beta, WinSCP before 6.2.2, Bitvise SSH Server before 9.32, Bitvise SSH Client before 9.33, KiTTY through 0.76.1.13, the net-ssh gem 7.2.0 for Ruby, the mscdex ssh2 module before 1.15.0 for Node.js, the thrussh library before 0.35.1 for Rust, and the Russh crate before 0.40.2 for Rust.

statements.status_notes: This is the Terrapin SSH handshake weakness: an attacker who can intercept and modify traffic between an SSH client and server can drop handshake messages and silently downgrade some connection security features when ChaCha20-Poly1305 or CBC with encrypt-then-MAC is negotiated. The bundled Apache MINA SSHD 2.9.2 is not part of the SonarQube server runtime; it ships only in the scanner engine that runs on the analysis machine, where it serves solely as an optional SSH client backend for Subversion SCM operations (blame and changed-file detection) over svn+ssh:// and is used only when the scanner JVM is started with -Dsvnkit.ssh.client=apache. When that option is used, exploitation still requires an active man-in-the-middle position between the analysis machine and the customer's Subversion server, so the risk is reduced but not eliminated.
statements.action_statement: Apache MINA SSHD versions before 2.12.0 are affected (2.12.0 adds strict key exchange on the client side). SonarQube Community Build 26.11 bundles 2.9.2 inside the scanner engine. Releases from 2026.4 onward bundle 2.9.2, while the 2026.1 LTA bundles 2.16.0. Customers using svn+ssh:// with -Dsvnkit.ssh.client=apache can mitigate by disabling chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com and either the CBC ciphers or the -etm@openssh.com MACs on their Subversion SSH server (connections continue to work, since the client also offers AES-CTR and AES-GCM), or by using an HTTPS Subversion URL. Customers not analyzing Subversion projects over svn+ssh:// with that option are not using this component.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-115715
vulnerability.description: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770) in Elasticsearch can lead to denial of service via a specially crafted input value that is processed by an affected phonetic encoder of the analysis-phonetic plugin. An authenticated user with permission to write documents to or run searches against an index that uses an affected encoder can cause an Elasticsearch node to exhaust its heap memory. The node can become unresponsive or terminate.

statements.status_notes: This flaw is in the phonetic encoders of the analysis-phonetic plugin and requires an index that uses an affected encoder. The analysis-phonetic plugin is not bundled with SonarQube's Elasticsearch, and no phonetic encoder is present in the search engine. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-115710
vulnerability.description: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information (CWE-524) in Elasticsearch can lead to information disclosure and incorrect search results via specially crafted search requests. For some query types, Elasticsearch can share cached query results between users who have field-level security restrictions and users who do not. A user restricted by field-level security can learn which documents match a value in a field that they cannot read. A restricted user can also cause users with full access to receive incomplete search results. Disclosure is only possible when a user with full access ran the same query on the same shard recently.

statements.status_notes: This flaw needs users restricted by field-level security and unrestricted users searching the same indices, and Elastic states that deployments that do not use field-level security are not affected. SonarQube does not use field-level security: Elasticsearch security is off on single-node installs, and in Data Center Edition it is either off or, when sonar.cluster.search.password is set, limited to the built-in account protected by that password, with no restricted roles defined. SonarQube user accounts are not Elasticsearch accounts. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-115298
vulnerability.description: Incorrect Authorization (CWE-863) in Elasticsearch can lead to information disclosure via Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs (CAPEC-1). An authenticated user whose index access is restricted by field-level security can retrieve the value of a constant_keyword field that their role excludes. Some search and query features do not apply the field-level security restriction to this field type.

statements.status_notes: This flaw lets a user whose index access is restricted by field-level security read a constant_keyword field that their role excludes. The bundled Elasticsearch does not ship the constant_keyword field type, and SonarQube defines no field-level security roles: Elasticsearch security is off on single-node installs, and in Data Center Edition it is either off or, when sonar.cluster.search.password is set, limited to the built-in account protected by that password. SonarQube user accounts are not Elasticsearch accounts. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-113602
vulnerability.description: json-smart through 2.6.0 contains an input validation bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to evade strict-mode trailing-data checks by inserting a literal 0x1A character. Attackers can append 0x1A and malformed content to pass JSONValue.parseStrict or isValidJsonStrict validation, creating parser differentials with downstream parsers like Jackson or Gson.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-113602 lets a literal 0x1A character hide trailing data from json-smart strict-mode checks, creating a difference between what json-smart accepts and what another parser reads. The bundled Elasticsearch carries this version twice. In its AI inference module (elasticsearch/modules/x-pack-inference), json-smart is used only by the Microsoft authentication library and the OAuth 2.0 library behind it to parse token responses from Microsoft Entra ID. In its security module (elasticsearch/modules/x-pack-security), it is used by the OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect library and Elasticsearch's OpenID Connect realm. Elasticsearch reads realm definitions from its node configuration file at startup, and the configuration SonarQube generates defines no realm (the application jar does not contain the string authc.realms). Nothing uses json-smart's validation result to decide whether other JSON is trusted, so the parsing difference has no security effect. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-106554
vulnerability.description:
One CBOR-parsing issue in jackson-dataformats-binary's CBOR module: an unbounded run of CBOR tags drives quadratic-time TagList growth (CPU/GC-exhaustion DoS, PoC-proven).



PoC executed against com.fasterxml.jackson.dataformat:jackson-dataformat-cbor:2.18.2; present in current 2.x and 3.x (tools.jackson.dataformat.cbor) HEAD. Distinct from the Avro and Smile/Protobuf advisories for this repo.



Quadratic CPU/GC DoS from an unbounded chain of CBOR tags (PoC-proven). File: cbor/src/main/java/.../cbor/CBORParser.java (tag handling -> TagList).



CBOR permits a data item to be preceded by any number of semantic tags. The CBOR parser accumulates them in a TagList whose backing array grows by a fixed increment (+8), not by doubling, and re-scans/copies on each growth. An attacker sends a value preceded by a long run of tag bytes; the fixed-increment growth makes accumulating N tags O(N^2) in time (plus GC pressure), with no cap on the number of stacked tags.



PoC (executed, JDK 17): feeding a CBOR stream consisting of a long run of tag bytes (e.g. tag 0xC0+) before a trivial value forces quadratic CPU/GC; parse time grows super-linearly with the tag count, pinning a request thread with no configurable limit.



Impact. Algorithmic-complexity denial of service (CWE-407): a modest input of stacked tags consumes quadratic CPU/GC, pinning a request thread; concurrent requests exhaust the pool.



Fix. Grow TagList by doubling and/or cap the number of stacked tags (StreamReadConstraints-style).

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-106554 is quadratic CPU and memory use in jackson-dataformat-cbor when parsing a CBOR document with a very long run of stacked tags; Elasticsearch accepts CBOR request bodies. These copies are in the bundled Elasticsearch content parsing library (elasticsearch/lib/elasticsearch-x-content-9.4.7.jar). SonarQube starts Elasticsearch with its HTTP port (sonar.search.port, default 9001) bound to the loopback address by default (sonar.search.host) and without authentication on that port, and Elasticsearch accepts cross-origin browser requests from any origin. A process on the SonarQube host can therefore send such a request, and so can a web page open in a browser on that host if the browser allows requests to the loopback address; SonarQube itself never does. The impact is memory or CPU exhaustion of the search process, so the risk is reduced but not eliminated.
statements.action_statement: SonarQube Community Build 26.11.0.134175 bundles Elasticsearch 9.4.7 with jackson-dataformat-cbor 2.18.9, which is affected (jackson-dataformat-cbor versions before 2.18.12, 2.21.8 and 2.22.4). SonarQube sets Elasticsearch cross-origin access unconditionally and has no setting to turn it off, and a firewall cannot separate the search port from a browser on the SonarQube host, so no configuration removes the exposure. To reduce it, do not browse untrusted web pages from the SonarQube host and keep sonar.search.host at its default loopback address so that other hosts cannot reach the port.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-102554
vulnerability.description: Allocation of resources without limits or throttling (CWE-770) during Java object deserialization in Google Guava versions 4.0 through 33.7.1 allows an attacker to cause a Denial of Service via OutOfMemoryError. When deserializing CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet, or MapMakerInternalMap instances, Guava eagerly allocates an array based on a caller-specified size parameter without throttling, permitting memory exhaustion from crafted serialization streams.

statements.status_notes: This issue affects Java deserialization of certain Guava collection classes, so it needs an ObjectInputStream reading attacker-supplied bytes. In SonarQube Community Build the only places the server constructs an ObjectInputStream read data the server wrote itself, to its database or to a local cache file, never data received from the network. Cluster mode is not available in this edition, and no remote management options are enabled on the server JVMs. The Python analyzer plugin also lists this Guava version but carries none of its collection classes. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-110591
vulnerability.description: OW2 ASM 1.4.3 before 9.11 contains an excessive resource consumption vulnerability in Analyzer.analyze() that allows attackers to exhaust memory and CPU via crafted class files. Attackers can supply class files analysed through BasicVerifier, SimpleVerifier or SourceInterpreter to trigger unbounded per-instruction Frame allocation and fix point iterations, causing denial of service.

statements.status_notes: This issue is in ASM's Analyzer when it runs the BasicVerifier, SimpleVerifier or SourceInterpreter on crafted class files. In the Painless scripting module, the only code that could use it is ASM's bytecode checker, and Painless configures that checker without data flow analysis, so the Analyzer never runs; no other class in the bundled search engine uses this copy. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-110270
vulnerability.description: OW2 ASM 3.0 before 9.11 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation vulnerability in the asm-commons JSRInlinerAdapter that inlines JSR/RET subroutines without memory or work limits. Attackers can supply a crafted class file with nested subroutines to force O(2^n) memory allocation, causing an OutOfMemoryError that crashes the JVM.

statements.status_notes: This issue is in the ASM JSRInlinerAdapter class, which inlines JSR subroutines of class files it reads. No class in the bundled search engine other than the Elasticsearch APM agent uses JSRInlinerAdapter. The agent uses the private copy of ASM bundled inside its own jar, not this one. Elasticsearch's launcher attaches the agent with a -javaagent option when it starts the search JVM. The apm module does not reference the JDK's agent attach API. The search JVM that SonarQube starts has no -javaagent option. Telemetry settings changed through the Elasticsearch HTTP API do not attach the agent, at run time or after a restart. The Painless scripting module uses only ASM's GeneratorAdapter and Method helpers to write its own bytecode, so the vulnerable code is never executed. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-110263
vulnerability.description: OW2 ASM 3.0 before 9.11 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in SignatureReader.parseType() that allows attackers to exhaust the stack via deeply nested generic type signatures. Attackers can supply a crafted class file with a long Signature attribute containing many nested type arguments to trigger a StackOverflowError during class transformation, causing denial of service.

statements.status_notes: This issue is recursion while ASM's SignatureReader parses a deeply nested generic signature in a crafted class file. The reported file is the ASM jar of the Elasticsearch plugin command line tool. Elasticsearch's startup loads this tool only to synchronize plugins from an elasticsearch-plugins.yml file, which SonarQube does not create and which Elasticsearch accepts only in its Docker distribution, so the step returns before any ASM code runs. In that tool ASM is used only to scan plugin jars during a plugin installation, which SonarQube never performs. No class in the bundled search engine other than the Elasticsearch APM agent calls SignatureReader. The agent calls the private copy of ASM bundled inside its own jar, not this one. Elasticsearch's launcher attaches the agent with a -javaagent option when it starts the search JVM. The apm module does not reference the JDK's agent attach API. The search JVM that SonarQube starts has no -javaagent option. Telemetry settings changed through the Elasticsearch HTTP API do not attach the agent, at run time or after a restart. The affected code therefore does not run. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-110261
vulnerability.description: OW2 ASM 3.0 before 9.11 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows attackers to exhaust CPU by supplying crafted class files processed with ClassWriter.COMPUTE_FRAMES. Attackers can craft methods that make the unbounded MethodWriter.computeAllFrames() fix point algorithm converge slowly, tying up transforming threads for unbounded time.

statements.status_notes: This issue is slow convergence of ASM's ClassWriter frame computation (COMPUTE_FRAMES) for crafted methods, which can tie up the transforming thread. The reported file is the ASM jar of the Elasticsearch plugin command line tool; no ASM code from it runs in SonarQube because SonarQube does not create an elasticsearch-plugins.yml file. An identical ASM 9.10.1 jar is loaded by the Elasticsearch Painless scripting module, which compiles scripts submitted through the Elasticsearch HTTP API and uses ASM's ClassWriter to compute frames for them. The same ASM jar is also loaded by the Elasticsearch security and AI inference modules, where only the accessors-smart library uses it, to generate small field accessor classes for Java classes chosen by the calling code; it never reads class files, generates no exception handlers and does not compute stack map frames, so request content cannot shape the generated code. SonarQube starts this Elasticsearch with its HTTP port (sonar.search.port, default 9001) bound to the host's loopback address by default (sonar.search.host), with no authentication, and Elasticsearch permits cross-origin browser requests, so a web page opened in a browser on the SonarQube host, or any process on that host, can submit such a script; SonarQube itself never submits scripts. It could not be ruled out that a crafted script makes the generated bytecode trigger this issue, so the risk is reduced but not eliminated.
statements.action_statement: SonarQube Server 2026.5.3 and 2026.5.4 and SonarQube Community Build 26.11 bundle Elasticsearch 9.4.7 with ASM 9.10.1, which is affected (ASM versions before 9.11). Keep sonar.search.host at its default loopback address and do not expose the search port (sonar.search.port, default 9001) beyond the SonarQube host. Elasticsearch on the SonarQube host cannot be firewalled from a browser or process on that host, so this reduces but does not remove the exposure.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-110260
vulnerability.description: OW2 ASM 3.0 before 9.11 contains a quadratic memory allocation vulnerability in MethodWriter.computeMaxStackAndLocal() and computeAllFrames() when using COMPUTE_MAXS or COMPUTE_FRAMES. Attackers can supply a crafted class file with thousands of overlapping exception handlers, causing excessive Edge allocations and an OutOfMemoryError that crashes the JVM.

statements.status_notes: This issue is quadratic memory allocation in ASM's ClassWriter when it computes maximum stack sizes or stack map frames for a method with thousands of overlapping exception handlers. The reported file is the ASM jar of the Elasticsearch plugin command line tool, which runs no ASM code in SonarQube, but an identical ASM 9.10.1 jar is loaded by the Elasticsearch Painless scripting module, which compiles scripts submitted through the Elasticsearch HTTP API and uses ASM's ClassWriter to compute frames for them. The same ASM jar is also loaded by the Elasticsearch security and AI inference modules, where only the accessors-smart library uses it, to generate small field accessor classes for Java classes chosen by the calling code; it never reads class files, generates no exception handlers and does not compute stack map frames, so request content cannot shape the generated code. SonarQube starts this Elasticsearch with its HTTP port (sonar.search.port, default 9001) bound to the host's loopback address by default (sonar.search.host), with no authentication, and Elasticsearch permits cross-origin browser requests, so a web page opened in a browser on the SonarQube host, or any process on that host, can submit such a script; SonarQube itself never submits scripts. It could not be ruled out that a crafted script makes the generated bytecode trigger this issue, so the risk is reduced but not eliminated.
statements.action_statement: SonarQube Server 2026.5.3 and 2026.5.4 and SonarQube Community Build 26.11 bundle Elasticsearch 9.4.7 with ASM 9.10.1, which is affected (ASM versions before 9.11). Keep sonar.search.host at its default loopback address and do not expose the search port (sonar.search.port, default 9001) beyond the SonarQube host. Elasticsearch on the SonarQube host cannot be firewalled from a browser or process on that host, so this reduces but does not remove the exposure.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-110258
vulnerability.description: OW2 ASM 3.0 before 9.11 contains an excessive memory allocation vulnerability in Label.addSubroutineRetSuccessors() that fails to enforce the single-RET-per-JSR rule. Attackers can supply a crafted invalid class file with multiple RET instructions for one JSR, triggering a roughly 2 GB allocation that crashes the JVM.

statements.status_notes: This issue is excessive memory allocation in ASM when a crafted class file has several RET instructions for one JSR subroutine. The reported file is the ASM jar of the Elasticsearch plugin command line tool. Elasticsearch's startup loads this tool only to synchronize plugins from an elasticsearch-plugins.yml file, which SonarQube does not create and which Elasticsearch accepts only in its Docker distribution, so the step returns before any ASM code runs. In that tool ASM is used only to scan plugin jars during a plugin installation, which SonarQube never performs. JSR subroutines reach ASM only through class files it reads or code that emits JSR instructions. Outside that tool, no class in the bundled search engine reads class files with this ASM copy, the entitlement instrumenter's own embedded copy reads only a fixed set of JDK classes, and neither the Painless compiler nor the accessors-smart library in the security and AI inference modules emits JSR instructions. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-110257
vulnerability.description: OW2 ASM 5.0 before 9.11 contains an excessive memory allocation vulnerability in ClassReader.readBootstrapMethodsAttribute() that sizes an int array from num_bootstrap_methods without validating attribute_length. Attackers can supply a crafted class file of about 100 bytes that forces roughly 2 GB allocation, causing an OutOfMemoryError that crashes the JVM or consuming thread.

statements.status_notes: This issue is excessive memory allocation in ASM's ClassReader when it reads the BootstrapMethods attribute of a crafted class file. The reported file is the ASM jar of the Elasticsearch plugin command line tool. Elasticsearch's startup loads this tool only to synchronize plugins from an elasticsearch-plugins.yml file, which SonarQube does not create and which Elasticsearch accepts only in its Docker distribution, so the step returns before any ASM code runs. In that tool ASM is used only to scan plugin jars during a plugin installation, which SonarQube never performs. Outside that tool, no class in the bundled search engine reads class files with this ASM copy. Elasticsearch's entitlement instrumenter embeds its own copy of the same ASM version but reads only a fixed set of JDK classes, and the Painless scripting module and the accessors-smart library in the security and AI inference modules only write their own bytecode and never read class files. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-118259
vulnerability.description: opentelemetry-java is the Java implementation of the OpenTelemetry API for recording telemetry, and SDK for managing telemetry recorded by the API. Prior to 1.67.0, W3CTraceContextPropagator.extract() uses regex delimiter processing that can exhibit quadratic backtracking while parsing tracestate headers containing long runs of spaces or tabs without a following comma. An unauthenticated attacker whose headers reach extraction can repeatedly block request or event-loop threads and cause excessive CPU consumption, with practical impact bounded by ingress header-size limits, proxy configuration, and threading. This issue is fixed in version 1.67.0.

statements.status_notes: This issue is slow regular expression processing in OpenTelemetry's W3CTraceContextPropagator.extract() when it parses an incoming tracestate header. In the bundled Elasticsearch this library ships in the APM telemetry module (elasticsearch/modules/apm). That module extracts trace headers when tracing is enabled. A request to the Elasticsearch HTTP API can enable tracing at run time. Without the APM agent, the module's tracer is the OpenTelemetry API's no-op implementation. Its propagator does not parse trace headers. No class in the bundled search engine other than the Elasticsearch APM agent installs this library's W3CTraceContextPropagator as a propagator (the library's only own reference is an unused SQL commenter helper inside OpenTelemetry itself). The agent builds its propagator from the private copy of the OpenTelemetry API bundled inside its own jar, not from this one. Elasticsearch's launcher attaches the agent with a -javaagent option when it starts the search JVM. The apm module does not reference the JDK's agent attach API. The search JVM that SonarQube starts has no -javaagent option. Telemetry settings changed through the Elasticsearch HTTP API do not attach the agent, at run time or after a restart. The vulnerable parser therefore does not run. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-107314
vulnerability.description: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, versions 42.7.11 through 42.7.13 enforce no restriction when the requireAuth connection property excludes all six authentication methods the driver knows, for example requireAuth=!password,!md5,!gss,!sspi,!scram-sha-256,!none. The driver then accepts any method the server asks for, including cleartext password authentication. A value without a method in it, such as requireAuth=, (a single comma), is affected the same way. An attacker positioned between the application and its server can ask for cleartext password authentication and receive the database password. A positive list such as requireAuth=scram-sha-256, and a partial exclusion such as requireAuth=!password,!md5, are enforced correctly. The property has no default value, so a deployment that does not set it is not affected. 42.7.14 fixes the problem: such a connection is refused with SQLState 08004, and a value without a method in it is rejected as invalid.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-107314 affects pgjdbc 42.7.11 through 42.7.13: if the requireAuth connection property excludes every authentication method the driver knows, or is a bare comma, the driver accepts any method the server requests, including cleartext password, so a man-in-the-middle between SonarQube and its database could collect the database password. The bundled 42.7.13 is in the affected range. SonarQube never sets requireAuth and the property has no default, so the flaw applies only if an administrator adds such a value to the database connection settings (sonar.jdbc.url or sonar.jdbc.dataSource properties), and exploiting it additionally needs an attacker positioned on the network path to the database.
statements.action_statement: pgjdbc versions before 42.7.14 are affected (from 42.7.14 the driver refuses such a connection and rejects an empty value). SonarQube Community Build 26.11.0.134175 bundles 42.7.13. Do not set requireAuth in the database connection settings, or set only a positive list such as requireAuth=scram-sha-256 (never an exclusion-only or empty value), and add sslmode=verify-full so the database server's certificate is verified, which removes the man-in-the-middle position this issue needs.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-107315
vulnerability.description: pgjdbc, the PostgreSQL JDBC Driver, versions 42.7.4 through 42.7.13 pads a value that is shorter than its declared length with bytes left in its send buffer instead of zeros, and the server stores those bytes as part of the value. The bytes are messages the driver sent earlier on the same connection: SQL text and parameter values of recent statements, which on a pooled connection can come from other requests. Each padded value can carry up to 8192 bytes of this traffic, or 16320 bytes on a connection with GSS encryption. The padding happens when an application declares a length larger than the data it supplies, through PreparedStatement.setObject with a ByteStreamWriter, CopyIn.writeToCopy, PGCopyOutputStream.write, LargeObject.write, or Blob.setBytes. The driver accepts these calls without an error. An attacker who can make the application store such a value and read it back can collect earlier traffic. Applications whose declared lengths always match their data are not affected. Versions 42.7.3 and earlier pad with zeros.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-107315 is an information disclosure in pgjdbc 42.7.4 through 42.7.13: when an application declares a value length larger than the data it supplies (through setObject with a ByteStreamWriter, CopyIn.writeToCopy, PGCopyOutputStream.write, LargeObject.write or Blob.setBytes), the driver pads the value with stale send-buffer bytes instead of zeros. No SonarQube or bundled plugin class references any driver-specific class or calls Blob.setBytes; SonarQube stores binary data only through standard JDBC calls whose length is either undeclared (the driver reads the whole stream) or taken from the exact byte array being written, and the driver's own stream-to-large-object copy writes exactly the bytes it read. The length mismatch the flaw needs never occurs. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-103008
vulnerability.description: Uncontrolled Recursion (CWE-674) in Elasticsearch can lead to Denial of Service via a specially crafted request that causes the server to construct and process a deeply nested data structure with no bound on recursion depth. Elasticsearch contains an uncontrolled recursion weakness in how it builds and serializes geometry values produced by scripted runtime fields. Unlike geometry supplied as text, which is subject to a nesting-depth limit, geometry constructed from a script's output is not bounded. An authenticated user with read access to a single index can submit a request defining such a field with a script that produces a deeply nested structure. Processing this request recurses past the available stack space, causing the affected node to terminate. The node does not recover automatically on all deployments and may require manual intervention to restore service.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-103008 is unbounded recursion when Elasticsearch builds and serializes geometry values produced by a script in a runtime field defined in a search request, and needs read access to one index. Elastic's advisory states that all configurations are affected. The geometry script support and the Painless scripting module are present in the bundled Elasticsearch. SonarQube starts this Elasticsearch with its HTTP port (sonar.search.port, default 9001) bound by default to the loopback address of the SonarQube host (sonar.search.host). That port has no authentication, and Elasticsearch accepts cross-origin browser requests from any origin, so any process on the SonarQube host, and also a web page open in a browser on that host, can send it requests without a SonarQube credential. SonarQube itself never sends such a request. The impact is a crash of the search process, so the risk is reduced but not eliminated.
statements.action_statement: SonarQube Server 2026.5.2, 2026.5.3 and 2026.5.4 and SonarQube Community Build 26.11 bundle Elasticsearch 9.4.7, and SonarQube Server 2026.1.7 and 2026.1.8 ship Elasticsearch 8.19.8; all are affected (Elasticsearch versions before 8.19.23 on the 8.19 line, 9.4.8 and 9.5.5). In Developer, Enterprise and Community editions the Elasticsearch HTTP port cannot be firewalled from a browser on the SonarQube host and the cross-origin setting cannot be changed. Keep sonar.search.host at its default so the port is not reachable from other hosts, and do not browse untrusted web pages from the SonarQube host, which reduces but does not remove the exposure.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-103005
vulnerability.description: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value (CWE-789) in Elasticsearch can lead to denial of service via Excessive Allocation (CAPEC-130). An authenticated user with connector management privileges could cause the cluster to allocate an uncontrolled amount of memory when connector resources with an excessively large `description` field are created and subsequently accessed, exhausting available heap memory and crashing the affected node.

statements.status_notes: The flaw is in the connector management resources used by Elastic's connectors feature and requires connector management privileges. The bundled Elasticsearch does not ship the connector APIs: no connector or other enterprise search application class exists in the search engine. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-102409
vulnerability.description: Uncontrolled Recursion (CWE-674) in Elasticsearch can allow an authenticated user with low privileges to terminate an Elasticsearch node, resulting in denial of service, via Excessive Allocation (CAPEC-130).

statements.status_notes: Elastic's advisory places this uncontrolled recursion in the text chunking functionality and names ES|QL as the exposed feature. The ES|QL query engine is not bundled with SonarQube's Elasticsearch. The same chunking code (org.elasticsearch.xpack.core.inference.chunking in x-pack-core) is also used by the inference APIs, which are present in the bundled Elasticsearch, so a client that can send requests to the search port could still reach it. SonarQube starts this Elasticsearch with its HTTP port (sonar.search.port, default 9001) bound by default to the loopback address of the SonarQube host (sonar.search.host). That port has no authentication, and Elasticsearch accepts cross-origin browser requests from any origin, so any process on the SonarQube host, and also a web page open in a browser on that host, can send it requests without a SonarQube credential. SonarQube itself never sends such a request. The impact is a crash or stall of the search process, so the risk is reduced but not eliminated.
statements.action_statement: SonarQube Server 2026.5.2, 2026.5.3 and 2026.5.4 and SonarQube Community Build 26.11 bundle Elasticsearch 9.4.7 (SonarQube Server 2026.5.0 and 2026.5.1 bundle 9.4.3), all in the affected range (Elasticsearch versions before 9.4.8 on the 9.4 line and before 9.5.5; the 8.x line is not affected). In Developer, Enterprise and Community editions the Elasticsearch HTTP port cannot be firewalled from a browser on the SonarQube host and the cross-origin setting cannot be changed. Keep sonar.search.host at its default so the port is not reachable from other hosts, and do not browse untrusted web pages from the SonarQube host, which reduces but does not remove the exposure.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-102408
vulnerability.description: Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity (CWE-1333) in Elasticsearch can lead to denial of service via Regular Expression Exponential Blowup (CAPEC-492). The ES|QL CHUNK function's recursive chunking strategy accepts a list of user-supplied regular expressions used as text-splitting separators, without validating their computational complexity or bounding their execution time. An authenticated user with read access to any text-based index can submit a specially crafted regular expression that triggers catastrophic backtracking, consuming excessive CPU on Elasticsearch worker threads and degrading query throughput for other tenants on the affected node. The cluster does not crash as a result of this issue.

statements.status_notes: This issue is catastrophic regular expression backtracking in the recursive text chunking strategy, which Elastic's advisory reaches through the ES|QL CHUNK function using separators supplied in a query. The ES|QL query engine is not bundled with SonarQube's Elasticsearch, so the CHUNK function does not exist. The same chunking code is also used by the inference APIs, which are present in the bundled Elasticsearch, so a client that can send requests to the search port could still reach it. In a single-node installation Elasticsearch listens on the loopback address by default (sonar.search.host) with no authentication, and it accepts cross-origin requests from web pages, so a web page opened in a browser on the SonarQube host, or any local process, can send requests to it. SonarQube itself never sends such a request. The impact is CPU exhaustion of the search process, so the risk is reduced but not eliminated.
statements.action_statement: SonarQube Server 2026.5.3 and 2026.5.4 and SonarQube Community Build 26.11.0 bundle Elasticsearch 9.4.7, and SonarQube Server 2026.1.8 ships Elasticsearch 8.19.8; both are affected (Elasticsearch versions before 8.19.22, 9.4.8 and 9.5.5). For single-node installations a firewall does not stop a browser running on the SonarQube host, and SonarQube offers no property to turn off the cross-origin setting or to add authentication outside Data Center Edition, so avoid opening untrusted web pages in a browser on the SonarQube server host.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-102404
vulnerability.description: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (CWE-400) in Elasticsearch can lead to denial of service via Excessive Allocation (CAPEC-130). A low-privileged authenticated user can submit a specially crafted query that causes uncontrolled memory growth in the query processing engine, resulting in an out-of-memory condition that terminates the Elasticsearch node. The condition can be triggered repeatedly, including by queries embedded in shared resources, causing persistent cluster unavailability.

statements.status_notes: Elastic's advisory places this uncontrolled memory growth in the ES|QL query engine and limits it to deployments where users can run ES|QL queries. The bundled Elasticsearch does not include the ES|QL query engine: only the small ES|QL core support library ships, and no ES|QL planner, compute engine, function or query action class is present in the search engine. Elasticsearch registers no handler for ES|QL queries: it rejects a POST request to the ES|QL endpoint (/_query) with HTTP status 405. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-71892
vulnerability.description: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, the opt-in key-size validation on CMS key-transport recipients, org.bouncycastle.cms.jcajce.JceKeyTransRecipient.setKeySizeValidation(true), never ran for a message using RFC 9709 content-encryption key derivation (id-alg-cek-hkdf-sha256). The branch that should have selected the actual content-encryption algorithm carried in the key derivation AlgorithmIdentifier's parameters compared the encrypted-key byte array against the id-alg-cek-hkdf-sha256 object identifier, a comparison between a byte array and an ASN1ObjectIdentifier that is false for every possible input, so the check fell through to a key-size lookup on the outer wrapper OID. That OID identifies a key-derivation construction rather than a cipher and has no registered key size, so the size comparison was skipped entirely. A key-transport EnvelopedData or AuthEnvelopedData whose transported, HKDF-derived content-encryption key did not match the key size of the advertised content-encryption algorithm was therefore accepted even with validation explicitly enabled, silently defeating the only mechanism the API offers for enforcing recovered key size. The recipient now dispatches on the content-encryption AlgorithmIdentifier's algorithm OID, so validation checks the recovered key against the inner content-encryption algorithm. Messages with a matching key size, non-HKDF messages, and recipients that do not enable validation are unaffected. This issue also affects Bouncy Castle for Java FIPS (BC-FJA) before bcpkix-fips 2.0.13 (2.0.X series) and 2.1.13 (2.1.X series).

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-71892 is a flaw in Bouncy Castle's CMS key-transport recipient, where the optional key-size validation never runs for RFC 9709 key derivation messages (fixed in 1.86). No code that can run with this jar on its classpath references the CMS classes or JceKeyTransRecipient. This jar sits only in the embedded Elasticsearch distribution's certificate-tool directory (elasticsearch/lib/tools/security-cli), which is not on the Elasticsearch server's module path. At each start the Elasticsearch launcher loads this directory only to run its security auto-configuration step, and that step exits before any Bouncy Castle code runs because SonarQube writes xpack.security.autoconfiguration.enabled=false and xpack.security.enabled=false into the Elasticsearch configuration; SonarQube never runs the directory's command line tools (certutil, certgen, reconfigure-node). Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-18040
vulnerability.description: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, HQC leaked secret-derived data through two side channels: its GF(2^8) arithmetic used lookup tables indexed by field elements, making the cache line touched a function of the operand, and its fixed-weight support sampler left its duplicate scan as soon as a collision was found and stored accepted positions at a secret index. Both run on secret inputs during encapsulation and decapsulation, and the sampler re-expands the secret key from its seed on every decapsulation, so an attacker able to observe cache behaviour or decapsulation timing can recover information about the HQC private key. The field arithmetic is now table-free and the sampler branch-free within a batch of candidates, with output and randomness consumption unchanged.

statements.status_notes: [sonarqube-26.11.0.134175/elasticsearch/lib/tools/security-cli/bcprov-jdk18on-1.85.jar] CVE-2026-18040 is a side-channel flaw in Bouncy Castle's HQC post-quantum implementation, which leaks secret-derived data through table lookups and early loop exit (fixed in 1.86). HQC must be selected explicitly by application code, and no code that can run with this jar on its classpath references the HQC classes. This jar sits only in the embedded Elasticsearch distribution's certificate-tool directory (elasticsearch/lib/tools/security-cli), which is not on the Elasticsearch server's module path. At each start the Elasticsearch launcher loads this directory only to run its security auto-configuration step, and that step exits before any Bouncy Castle code runs because SonarQube writes xpack.security.autoconfiguration.enabled=false and xpack.security.enabled=false into the Elasticsearch configuration; SonarQube never runs the directory's command line tools (certutil, certgen, reconfigure-node). Not exploitable. [sonarqube-26.11.0.134175/elasticsearch/lib/tools/plugin-cli/elasticsearch-plugin-cli-bc-9.4.7.jar] CVE-2026-18040 is a side-channel flaw in the Bouncy Castle HQC post-quantum implementation. In SonarQube Community Build 26.11, Bouncy Castle 1.85 is bundled in elasticsearch/lib/tools/plugin-cli/elasticsearch-plugin-cli-bc-9.4.7.jar, a helper of the embedded Elasticsearch elasticsearch-plugin command. Its class outside Bouncy Castle (PgpSignatureVerifier) checks the PGP signature of a plugin archive downloaded from Elastic, and its caller is the plugin installation action. That action runs for elasticsearch-plugin install and for the plugin synchronization step, which installs the plugins listed in config/elasticsearch-plugins.yml, a file SonarQube does not ship. At each Elasticsearch start the server CLI puts lib/tools/plugin-cli, including this jar, on the class loader of its plugin synchronization step. Without config/elasticsearch-plugins.yml that step installs no plugin, so no Bouncy Castle code in this jar runs. Even during a manual installation the jar only verifies an OpenPGP signature over the downloaded archive against the Elastic public key, so HQC is never used. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-17508
vulnerability.description: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, several password-based key derivation entry points ran the KDF with cost parameters taken from the untrusted input being processed, without bounding them, so a small input could dictate an arbitrary amount of work before any password or integrity check could reject it. The affected paths are the RFC 9579 PBMAC1 MAC calculator builders, which took the PBKDF2 iteration count and derived-key length straight out of PBMAC1Params (JcePBMac1CalculatorBuilder, and PKCS12PBEUtils.createPBMac1Calculator reached from PKCS12PfxPdu.isMacValid); the scrypt parallelization parameter p in the PKCS#8 and PKCS#12 cost guards, which bounded only the cost parameter N and the block size r even though the scratch buffer scales with r times p, so the configured memory ceiling could be evaded entirely; the raw JCA PBKDF2 provider (org.bouncycastle.jcajce.provider.symmetric.PBEPBKDF2); and the bcrypt round count read from an encrypted OpenSSH v1 private key's own kdfoptions. Each now bounds the parameter before deriving, in line with the caps already applied elsewhere in the tree, with the OpenSSH round count configurable through the new org.bouncycastle.openssh.max_rounds property. This completes the bounding begun in 1.85 for the PKCS#8 / PBES2 decryptors (CVE-2026-15055). This issue also affects Bouncy Castle for Java LTS before 2.73.13, and Bouncy Castle for Java FIPS (BC-FJA) before bcpkix-fips 1.0.13 (1.0.X series), 2.0.13 (2.0.X series) and 2.1.13 (2.1.X series).

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-17508 is a denial-of-service flaw in several Bouncy Castle password-based key-derivation entry points (PBMAC1 MAC builders, the PKCS#8/PKCS#12 scrypt cost guards, the raw JCA PBKDF2 provider and OpenSSH key bcrypt rounds), which run the derivation with a cost taken from the untrusted input being processed (fixed in 1.86). No code that can run with this jar on its classpath references these classes; the Elasticsearch certificate tools use only the PEM encryptor, which chooses its own parameters. This jar sits only in the embedded Elasticsearch distribution's certificate-tool directory (elasticsearch/lib/tools/security-cli), which is not on the Elasticsearch server's module path. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-93566
vulnerability.description: A flaw was found in Netty. A remote attacker could exploit this by sending a specially crafted HTTP request that includes control characters within the chunk-size line. This bypasses the intended strict validation, allowing the attacker to inject arbitrary HTTP requests. This vulnerability can lead to HTTP request smuggling, potentially resulting in information disclosure or other unauthorized actions.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-93566 is a request-smuggling flaw in Netty's HTTP/1.1 request decoder: a chunk-size line containing a bare carriage return is accepted instead of rejected. That decoder runs in the HTTP listener of the Elasticsearch 9.4.7 search engine that SonarQube Community Build 26.11 starts (elasticsearch/modules/transport-netty4), but request smuggling only has an effect when a proxy, gateway or other intermediary in front of the server frames requests differently from Netty. SonarQube's web and Compute Engine processes connect directly to this listener with no intermediary in between, so there is no second parser whose request framing could disagree with Netty's. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-93565
vulnerability.description: A flaw was found in Netty RtspDecoder. The `RtspMethods.valueOf()` function incorrectly strips trailing control bytes from method tokens in Real-Time Streaming Protocol (RTSP) requests. A remote attacker can exploit this by sending a specially crafted RTSP request, leading to method-token smuggling. This vulnerability allows an attacker to bypass method-based access controls and can also be used to launder malicious requests through Netty-based RTSP proxies, making them appear legitimate to backend systems.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-93492
vulnerability.description: A flaw was found in Netty's HTTP/2 HpackEncoder. A remote attacker can exploit this by sending HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames with a very large MAX_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE. This causes the HpackEncoder to store an excessive number of unique headers, leading to increased CPU usage and memory consumption, ultimately resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-93492 is a resource-exhaustion flaw in Netty's HTTP/2 HpackEncoder when the peer announces a very large header table size in a SETTINGS frame. The netty-codec-http2 library is bundled only in Elasticsearch's AI inference module, where it is used by outbound HTTP clients (the AWS SDK client for Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker, and the Reactor Netty client behind the Azure SDK). Elasticsearch's own HTTP listener is HTTP/1.1 only, so no HTTP/2 connection is ever accepted. Those clients exist only after an inference endpoint for one of those services is defined, and SonarQube itself never defines inference endpoints. SonarQube starts this Elasticsearch with its HTTP port (sonar.search.port, default 9001) bound to the host's loopback address by default (sonar.search.host) and without authentication on that port, and Elasticsearch permits cross-origin browser requests, so a web page opened in a browser on the SonarQube host, or any process on that host, can send it requests; SonarQube itself never sends such a request. Exploitation also requires a malicious or compromised HTTP/2 server at the other end of that connection. The impact is memory exhaustion of the search process, so the risk is reduced but not eliminated.

vulnerability.description: A flaw was found in Netty's HTTP/2 stack. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to inject prohibited characters, such as NUL, Line Feed, and Carriage Return, into HTTP/2 header field values due to insufficient validation. When these values cross an HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 translation boundary, they can be exploited for request smuggling, header injection, or response splitting. vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-124077
vulnerability.description:

Only applications that build trees from names supplied by other sources, such as entries of archive formats that permit NUL bytes in names (e.g. ZIP) or names passed directly to the API, are exposed.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.23.0, which fixes the issue.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-119078
vulnerability.description:
Apache Commons Codec's Blake3 class documented the output of its doFinalize methods as depending on any previously finalized bytes, so that consecutive calls would return different output. In fact, doFinalize does not change the hash state: calling it again without supplying more input returns the same bytes. The key-derivation example in the class Javadoc, shipped since 1.16.0, derives two keys with two consecutive doFinalize calls. Code that follows it gets identical keys, so the separation between the derived keys is lost. The same applies to any application that calls doFinalize more than once on one instance and expects new output each time.



This issue affects Apache Commons Codec from 1.16.0 before 1.23.0.

Users should check their applications for repeated doFinalize calls on the same Blake3 instance and derive multiple keys by requesting the combined length in one call and splitting the output, as the updated Javadoc shows.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-89407
vulnerability.description:

An attacker who can supply JSON that an application deserializes into a numeric target type reaches this method through jackson-databind's default String-to-number coercion (StdDeserializer and NumberDeserializers for BigDecimal, BigInteger, Double and Float).

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-68494
vulnerability.description:
The fix released in jackson-core 2.18.6 and 2.21.1 for CVE-2026-18401 (GHSA-72hv-8253-57qq, number length constraint bypass in the non-blocking parser) is incomplete. This record covers the remaining bypass.

The earlier fix wired validateIntegerLength() into a new _setIntLength() helper and invoked it wherever the integer portion of a number is decided: a terminator byte arrives, a '.' or 'e'/'E' is seen, or input ends inside a fully buffered value. It was not invoked on the attacker-relevant path where the parser runs out of input while still inside the MINOR_NUMBER_INTEGER_DIGITS minor state and returns NOT_AVAILABLE to the caller.

As a result, an attacker who streams JSON to a non-blocking parser in many small chunks, without ever sending a terminator byte, keeps the parser inside MINOR_NUMBER_INTEGER_DIGITS indefinitely. _textBuffer.expandCurrentSegment() grows the accumulator on every chunk while validateIntegerLength() is never called. The accumulator is bounded only by maxStringLength (20 MiB by default) rather than by maxNumberLength (1000 by default), an amplification of roughly 20,000x over the documented limit. Because Java char values occupy two bytes, a single connection can be driven to approximately 40 MiB of heap before the validator finally fires when the value completes.

The equivalent fraction-path code is correct: _finishFloatFraction() calls _setFractLength() before its NOT_AVAILABLE return. The missing call affects the integer-digit paths in _startPositiveNumber(), _startNegativeNumber() and _finishNumberIntegralPart() in NonBlockingUtf8JsonParserBase.

Node's native WHATWG `URL` (used by `fetch()`, `undici`, and Node's `http`/`https` clients) instead treats `\` as interchangeable with `/` for special schemes (`http`, `https`, `ws`, `wss`, `ftp`, `file`), so the two parsers extract different hosts from the same input.

statements.status_notes: This issue is in fast-uri's URI parsing, normalization and comparison functions, so it needs an application to pass attacker-supplied URIs to them and rely on the result. In the JavaScript/TypeScript analyzer, the fast-uri code is not included in the analyzer's executable: the only Ajv version that depends on it is used by the stylelint CSS linter's output formatting helper, which runs validators compiled in advance from its own fixed schemas, and those validators do not use it. Not exploitable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-75899
vulnerability.description: fast-uri vulnerable to server-side request forgery via repeated hostname percent-decoding. `fast-uri` decodes a hostname's percent escapes twice in a single `normalize()` or `resolve()` call: once during parsing and again during authority recomposition. A nested percent-encoded host therefore survives the first decode and is turned into a live destination by the second, so `normalize('http://%256c%256f%2563%2561%256c%2568%256f%2573%2574/')` returns `http://localhost/`. Applications that normalize or resolve an untrusted URI before an SSRF check, redirect validation, or host allowlist can be steered to a different destination, including internal addresses such as loopback or a cloud metadata endpoint, than the encoded input appeared to contain. This is an incomplete-fix variant of CVE-2026-6322, whose encoded-authority-delimiter fix introduced the second decode.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-75975
vulnerability.description: fast-uri vulnerable to server-side request forgery via malformed IPv6 normalization. `fast-uri` does not validate the complete RFC 3986 grammar for bracketed IPv6 literals, so a malformed literal with invalid trailing text is silently truncated to a different valid IPv6 address with no error reported. For example, `normalize('http://[::not-valid]/private')` returns `http://[::]/private`, and `[fc00::not-hex]` and `[fe80::not-hex]` collapse to `[fc00::]` and `[fe80::]`. An application that normalizes an untrusted URL before an outbound request, redirect, or host-policy check can be routed to a local or private address such as loopback (`::1`), unique-local, or link-local. Because `parse().error` is unset for these inputs, checking it does not protect the consumer.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-84292
vulnerability.description: fast-uri vulnerable to authority injection via an unvalidated port in serialize. `fast-uri` serializes the `port` component of a URI without validating it. When recomposing the authority, `fast-uri` escapes the userinfo and host components but concatenates the port verbatim, so a `port` value that is not a sequence of digits can inject authority delimiters. vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-86472
vulnerability.description: fast-uri vulnerable to inconsistent host case normalization via percent-encoded octets. `fast-uri` folds the host to lowercase before it percent-decodes the host, so a percent-encoded uppercase unreserved octet such as `%41` decodes to a literal `A` that is never folded. For a scheme-relative reference (`//host`) there is no scheme, so the host canonicalization that repairs this on a scheme-bearing URL does not run. As a result `parse`, `normalize`, and `equal` disagree on the same host: `parse("//%41.com").host` returns `"A.com"` while `parse("//a.com").host` and `parse("//A.com").host` return `"a.com"`, and `equal("//%41.com", "//a.com")` is `false` even though `equal("//A.com", "//a.com")` is `true`. An application that makes a case-sensitive host decision on `fast-uri` output for a scheme-relative reference, for example a host allowlist or denylist that compares `parse(url).host` or uses `fast-uri.equal`, can be steered past the check with a percent-encoded uppercase octet. Because a hostname is case-insensitive in DNS and HTTP routing, the evading spelling reaches the same host the check meant to gate, so the effect is check evasion rather than reaching a different registrable host.
